title: Removal of the External Bonded Doubler Strap from the Fwd Lower Shell Lap Joint

issue.reason: Issue B. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: Removal of the externally bonded and riveted doubler strap from the forward lower shell longitudinal lap joint, used when the strap is damaged or when access to the underlying joint is needed for a structural assessment.

sections.purpose: This task removes the external bonded doubler strap from the forward lower shell lap joint between stations 1080 and 1360 on one side of the aircraft, so that the underlying joint can be inspected or repaired.
sections.job_setup_note: The aircraft must be on jacks with the landing gear extended and the ground locks fitted. The strap is bonded as well as riveted, so a controlled heat input is required to soften the adhesive line. Keep a fire watch during the heating operation. Do not lift the strap with a wedge before the adhesive is soft, because the skin beneath is only 1.6 millimetres thick and will deform.
sections.procedure: 1. Put the aircraft on jacks and install the ground locks. 2. Put the warning notices in the flight compartment and at the nose gear. WARNING: MAKE SURE THAT THE AIRCRAFT IS CORRECTLY SUPPORTED BEFORE YOU START WORK BELOW THE LOWER SHELL. 3. Remove the paint from the strap MOD50333-97 and from a 50 millimetre band around it. 4. Record the position of each fastener on the layout sheet before removal. 5. Remove the rivets AES645587-2A with the offset drill and a pilot bit, then punch out the shanks. CAUTION: DO NOT LET THE DRILL BREAK THROUGH INTO THE SKIN BENEATH. USE THE DEPTH STOP SET TO THE STRAP THICKNESS. 6. Attach the heater blanket to the strap and raise the adhesive line to the temperature given in the referenced repair data. 7. Monitor the skin temperature with the thermocouple set and do not exceed the stated limit. 8. Lift the strap progressively from the aft end with the nylon wedge set as the adhesive softens. 9. Remove the adhesive residue from the skin with the approved solvent and a plastic scraper. 10. Do a detailed visual inspection of the exposed joint and the splice plate ORV288354-46 and record every finding. 11. Do an eddy current inspection of both fastener rows before any further work.
sections.close_out: Protect the exposed joint with a temporary sealant if the aircraft is to be left overnight. Remove the heater blanket and the thermocouples. Remove the tools and the waste material from the area. Make an entry in the aircraft technical log that the strap has been removed and that the aircraft must not be released to service until the strap is reinstalled or a repair is approved.

safety_precautions: Put the aircraft on jacks and install the ground locks.
Put the warning notices in the flight compartment.
Keep a fire watch during the heating operation.
Wear eye protection during rivet removal.

tooling.description: Drill jig, lap joint fastener pattern
